narrative:
The model determined that you have a 52% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeds the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were your savings, the purpose of the loan, and the status of your checking account. Your savings of 1,000 DM or more was the single most important reason the model leaned toward approval. Having this level of savings is rare among approved applicants and pushed your prediction noticeably toward good credit. Unfortunately, the other two key factors worked against you and proved stronger overall.

The fact that you are requesting the loan to buy a new car pulled the prediction toward bad credit risk. Among people who received loans, far more borrowed for radio/TV or furniture than for new cars, so this purpose is associated with higher risk in the model. Similarly, your checking account balance in the 0–200 DM range also increased the predicted risk. While many approved applicants have no checking account at all, the model views a small positive balance in this specific range as less favorable than having a larger balance or no account.

In short, although your solid savings helped, the combination of a new-car purchase and your current checking-account level signaled enough risk to tip the decision against approval.

**What you should do next:** Consider reapplying with a different loan purpose, such as home-related improvements, or wait until your checking account shows a stronger balance. Either change could meaningfully improve your chances. (248 words)
